subject: Next steps & legal routing for ClearSight pilot (NDA/MSA/DPA)
messages:

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — ClearSight pilot (NDA/MSA/DPA)

Hi Emma / Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciated the clarity on use cases and decision criteria. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on procurement/legal routing: 

Key decision criteria you called out:
- Latency SLA for inference (95th pctl)
- Data residency (US-only for PHI)
- Cost per 1k inference units and predictable throughput for peak windows
- Security posture (SOC 2 + penetration test evidence)

Suggested legal/contract sequencing (typical for pilots):
1) Mutual NDA via DocuSign (clears the ability to share SOC2 and technical details) — target 3–5 business days
2) MSA redline (we can share a starter MSA + our redline guidelines) — target initial pass 7–10 business days after NDA
3) DPA reviewed in parallel with MSA (we try to run this concurrently to avoid extra loopbacks)
4) Procurement / PO issuance once signatures complete

Ask for you: can you confirm the primary owners for each item above at ClearSight (NDA owner, MSA owner/redlines, procurement contact)? Also, any internal turn-time expectations we should hit for each step?

I've attached a starter MSA redline and our redline guidelines for legal to review. I’ll loop in our legal lead to own the redline thread. Neha from security will follow up separately on the questionnaire.

Attachments: redline_msa_v1.docx; redline_guidelines.pdf

Next tangible steps from Redwood:
- Send DocuSign NDA link (today)
- Connor (legal) will pick up MSA redline once NDA is in flight
- Neha will share SOC2 artifacts and the security intake link

Thanks — happy to schedule a short legal-focused sync if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
Note: Redwood will protect PHI and supports customer-managed KMS for private deployments; happy to include a short security appendix in the MSA if useful.

Thanks Marissa / Emma — I’m on it. A few notes from legal to help speed things: 

1) NDA: standard mutual NDA via DocuSign is fine — we’ll consent to redaction of SOC2 where needed.
2) MSA sequencing: we’ll provide a redline that focuses on the key commercial and liability blocks (limits of liability, indemnity, data ownership, termination for convenience). If Sam is willing, proposing a single consolidated redline (not iterative line-by-line) reduces back-and-forth and shortens total review time.
3) DPA: we can push the DPA content as an exhibit to the MSA to run in parallel; if there are high-risk PHI clauses, we can flag them up front.

I attached our internal redline guidelines (highlights: preferred clause language, common concessions, and expected turn-times). If possible, can ClearSight mark any non-starters up front (e.g., unusual insurance caps, non-US data transfers) so we can target negotiation efficiently.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
